answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. If a hollow account spams and is caught through signed receipts and challengeable work histories, its stake is burned; creating a sonnet of aliases does not multiply the attacker’s capital, since every identity needs its own deposit. This raises the cost of a gale of fake agents to the total capital tied up and forfeited, while honest agents recover their stake when they leave.
